summary: Wenger's Image-Streaming asks the practitioner to close the eyes and describe aloud, rapidly and in sensory detail, whatever is seen. The 'Back-Up Procedures' are written for people who at first get no pictures at all: he claims none of thousands has gone through them without success and says he himself once could not visualise. Starters include a partner watching for eye movements, staring at a light or bright window and then describing the after-image as it changes, describing blobs of colour behind closed lids, and other bridging tricks; the after-image is said to turn gradually into other imagery once the describing is kept up.
why_relevant: Among the most explicit non-lineage instructions addressed to people who see nothing, using a physical afterimage as the bridge to self-sustaining imagery. Much of the later imagery is called 'mind's eye', so the reading agent must judge mode.
